clue.text: Footsie, expressing Deft "X", suggests how to locate here?

parts.note: the answer read as instructions says put the letters F and T inside the letters D, E and X, which spells the quoted words

explanation.surface: A guide on how to find the FTSE share index in this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as the instruction 'FT in DEX' and you get DE(FT)X, the quoted words. Footsie is the nickname of the FTSE 100 share index, once called the FT Index.
explanation.definitionFit: Footsie is the familiar name for the Financial Times stock market index.

clue.text: Accepted a blessing in disguise that may be referred

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for accepted, as written on a bill of exchange

indicators.note: something in disguise has its appearance altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Taking on something as a blessing in disguise that can be passed on to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disguise' looks like part of the stock phrase 'a blessing in disguise', but it signals the anagram of A BLESSING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something assignable can be attributed or referred to a particular cause or person.

clue.text: 7 10, this hit ground with absurdity

definitions.note: the cross-reference stands for the phrase at 7 down and 10 across, meaning wearing nothing

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A naked state, the clue suggests, came about when someone hit the ground absurdly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is the anagram signal for HIT plus ABSURDITY; 'this' and 'with' just join the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions are humorous idioms for being naked, as on the day of one's birth.

clue.text: Au naturel: later, a la mode, dishabille (SA being active at night!)

definitions.note: a nocturnal creature of South America, the abbreviation SA standing for the continent

indicators.note: a la mode means in fashion, so the letters are refashioned into a new arrangement
dishabille is a state of undress, so the letters of later are stripped away from those of Au naturel

explanation.surface: French phrases for nakedness and fashion, with a parenthetical aside about South America at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of AU NATUREL, strip out the letters of LATER ('dishabille', after 'a la mode' remodels LATER), and U, N, A, U remain. The unau is the two-toed sloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-toed sloth lives in South American forests and feeds by night.

clue.text: 12 little fellow follows when Number 100 comes round

definitions.note: the cross-reference stands for the answer at 12 across, meaning naked

indicators.note: comes round says the word for a hundred wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a ton is slang for a hundred

indicators.note: follows says the word for a small person comes after the word for when

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a titch is a small person

explanation.surface: A small man trails behind as the hundredth arrival turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes round' wraps the hundred around the other two pieces, and 'follows' puts the small person after 'when'. Titch is British slang for a small person; a ton is a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions are colloquial ways of saying wearing no clothes at all.

clue.text: Alan Turing's heart flutters, attaching not all blame for having 23 tendencies

indicators.note: flutters means moves about erratically, so the central letters are jumbled
the heart of the name is its core once the outer letters are trimmed
not all means the word for blame loses its final letter

parts.note: to take stick is to take blame or criticism

explanation.surface: Alan Turing's heart races as part of the blame is attached to him.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of ALAN TURING, ANTURI, is jumbled by 'flutters'; STICK with 'not all' loses K, giving STIC. 23 across is the naked enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturism is the practice of going unclothed, so a naturistic outlook leans that way.

clue.text: Brings up what 23s don't hide but derriere and arse, put together, do

indicators.note: put together says the end of one word is joined to the start of the next to show the hidden letters
do completes 'don't hide but ... do', so these words do hide the answer

explanation.surface: A cheeky note that naturists show their bottoms rather than hiding them.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the end of 'derriere' and the start of 'arse' once the two are put together, skipping 'and'. 23s are nudists.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to raise or bring them up.

clue.text: See 7
Noble, noble gas will

parts.note: AR is the chemical symbol for argon, a noble gas
'is to' expresses future intention, as will does

explanation.surface: A noble gas will do something, the clue begins and breaks off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble' appears twice: the first is the definition, the second part of 'noble gas'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aristo is a colloquial shortening for an aristocrat, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: 23 is made of sterner stuff for a start

definitions.note: the cross-reference stands for the answer at 23 across, a naked person; the answer is the adjective describing such a person

parts.note: stark means harsh or severe, so starker is sterner

indicators.note: for a start points to the opening letter of the word stuff

explanation.surface: A nudist proves tougher than they look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made of sterner stuff' is a stock phrase, but sterner gives STARKER and 'for a start' takes the S of stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Starkers is British slang for completely naked, the state of a naturist.

clue.text: Caught in drift, Mr E is exercising muscle

indicators.note: Caught in says the scrambled letters sit inside the word for drift

parts.note: the tenor of an argument is its drift or general sense

indicators.note: exercising means working out, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Mr E, caught in a current, exercises a muscle to stay afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr E is' looks like a person's name, but 'exercising' rearranges those letters, and 'Caught in' places them in the word for drift. The teres minor is a rotator cuff muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: The teres minor is a small shoulder muscle of the rotator cuff.

clue.text: At intervals unsubdued?

indicators.note: at intervals points to every other letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A question about something that is uninhibited only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of UNSUBDUED gives the answer, and being naked now and then is, the clue suggests, an unrestrained state.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unclothed is a kind of unrestrained, unsubdued exposure, as the whole clue hints.

clue.text: Hipsters Incorporated not all boisterous

parts.note: INC is the abbreviation for incorporated, used after a company name

indicators.note: not all says the word for boisterous loses its final letter

parts.note: rowdy means noisy and boisterous

explanation.surface: A trendy company is described as a little boisterous.
explanation.walkthrough: ROWDY with 'not all' loses its final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Hipsters are fashionable people, the trendy clique of the moment.

clue.text: Modern house the wife and I erected in rejuvenated Dublin

indicators.note: in says the upturned pair goes inside the rearranged letters
rejuvenated means made new again, so the letters of the city are remade
erected means put upright, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the wife and I together make we

explanation.surface: A couple build a modern home in a revitalised Dublin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns the couple's word upwards (this is a down clue), and 'in' places it among the remade letters of the city, signalled by 'rejuvenated'.
explanation.definitionFit: A new build is a recently constructed property, as opposed to an older one.

clue.text: Means to carry corrosive chaps to service?

parts.note: a car is something taken in for a service
boys is an informal word for chaps or men

explanation.surface: A question about whether caustic fellows are fit to serve.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'corrosive chaps', but 'corrosive' ends the definition; 'chaps to service' are car boys, lads who look after cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A carboy is a large protected glass bottle used for holding acids and other corrosive liquids.

clue.text: 14 entertained us and made merry

definitions.note: the cross-reference stands for the answer at 14 across, meaning unclothed

indicators.note: made merry means revelled, so the letters are thrown about in festive disorder

explanation.surface: A naked performer kept the audience amused and had fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made merry' signals the anagram of ENTERTAINED, US and AND.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a humorous idiom for being unclothed, in one's natural state.

clue.text: Junior ambassador worried about army check

indicators.note: about says the word for worried goes round the other pieces

parts.note: ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
CH is the abbreviation for check in chess notation

explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'army check' is an inspection, but the two words give separate abbreviations; 'about' wraps the word for worried round them.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a junior member of an embassy staff.

clue.text: Rock musical's not Harry Hill's concern!

clue.text: Is he out of pants? I dunno, from behind …

the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

explanation.walkthrough: The letters TSIDUN sit inside 'pants? I dunno', and 'from behind' reads them backwards. 'Is he out of pants?' loosely describes the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist is someone who comes out without clothes, out of their trousers.

clue.text: … a bod's 2, say, well turned out in my 5 1!

explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange A, BODS, the answer to 2 down (IN THE RAW) and SAY ('well turned out'). The leading dots continue from 23 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes being naked, as one is at birth; the definition means dressed only in one's skin.

clue.text: Competent looking up part of Tuscany?

indicators.note: looking up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: able means competent

explanation.surface: A capable person surveys a region of Tuscany.
explanation.walkthrough: ABLE read upwards ('looking up') gives the island.
explanation.definitionFit: The island where Napoleon was exiled belongs to the Italian region of Tuscany.
